name: Chicken Mandi
assumptions: Yield estimated from typical Chicken Mandi recipes using 1 kg chicken and 400 g rice, which commonly serves 4 adults as a main dish.

Preparation time estimated from step durations: marinating 15 min, rice soak 30 min, frying/browning 15 min, simmering chicken 20 min, cooking rice 15 min, steaming 15 min, optional smoking 10 min; overlaps and total active + passive time rounded to 90 min.
Ghee is mentioned as optional alternative to oil; dairy-free marked null because ghee presence is ambiguous/optional.
Sesame marked null because unspecified compound sauces (e.g. chutney or raita in serving suggestion) may contain sesame but are not confirmed in core ingredients.
instructions:
1. Clean and cut the chicken; marinate briefly with salt, turmeric and a little oil.
2. Rinse and soak basmati rice 20–30 minutes.
3. In a large pot, heat ghee/oil. Fry chopped onion until golden. Add minced garlic and green chillies and fry 1–2 min.
4. Add whole spices (cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, bay leaves) and ground spices (coriander, cumin). Stir until fragrant.
5. Add chicken pieces, brown lightly and add enough water/chicken stock to cover. Simmer until chicken is nearly cooked.
6. Remove chicken; measure remaining liquid and add soaked rice. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover and cook rice until almost done.
7. Return the chicken to the rice pot on top, cover tightly and steam on low for 10–15 min so flavors meld.
8. (Optional) For authentic smoky aroma: heat a small charcoal until red hot, place it on a small foil cup in the centre of the pot, add a tsp of butter/oil on the coal then cover immediately to trap smoke for 5–10 minutes. Remove coal.
9. Garnish with fried onions, chopped coriander and serve with chutney or raita.

ingredients.name: Chicken
ingredients.assumptions: 1 whole chicken assumed at 1000 g edible raw weight with skin and bone; typical for a medium bird in Indian recipes

ingredients.name: Basmati Rice
ingredients.assumptions: Standard dry basmati rice; 1 cup ≈ 200 g, so 2 cups = 400 g uncooked weight

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.assumptions: 4 cups water assumed at 240 ml per cup; water adds no macros

ingredients.name: Onion
ingredients.assumptions: 1 large onion ≈ 150 g raw peeled weight

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.assumptions: 1½ tsp table salt ≈ 9 g; adds negligible macros beyond sodium

ingredients.name: Oil
ingredients.assumptions: 3 tbsp neutral oil (e.g. vegetable) ≈ 41 g total; used for frying and marinating

ingredients.name: Turmeric Powder
ingredients.assumptions: 1 tbsp turmeric powder ≈ 7 g; typical ground spice density

ingredients.name: Coriander
ingredients.assumptions: 1 tsp ground coriander ≈ 2 g; spice weight

ingredients.name: Cardamom
ingredients.assumptions: ½ tbsp whole cardamom pods ≈ 3 g; typical whole spice measure

ingredients.name: Cloves
ingredients.assumptions: ¼ tsp whole cloves ≈ 1 g; typical whole spice measure

ingredients.name: Cinnamon
ingredients.assumptions: ½ tsp ground cinnamon ≈ 1.3 g; typical spice measure

ingredients.name: Pepper
ingredients.assumptions: 1 tsp ground black pepper ≈ 2 g; typical spice measure

ingredients.name: Bay Leaf
ingredients.assumptions: 2 bay leaves ≈ 1.2 g dry weight; typical whole leaf measure
